stories.headline: Iran's IRGC claims cruise-missile strike destroyed Amazon AWS data hub in Bahrain

key_facts.fact: Iran's IRGC Aerospace Force claimed on Tuesday (July 21) it targeted and 'destroyed' Amazon Web Services' central data infrastructure in Bahrain with multiple cruise missiles, as part of Wave 24 of 'Operation Nasr 2'.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) on Tuesday claimed that its Aerospace Force had targeted and destroyed Amazon Web Services' (AWS) central data infrastructure in Bahrain using several cruise missiles.

key_facts.fact: The IRGC said the strike was retaliation for a US attack Sunday on the under-construction Darkhovin nuclear facility in Iran's Khuzestan province, which Tehran describes as a civilian, IAEA-safeguarded project.
key_facts.excerpt: The Guard described the strike as a direct response to a U.S. attack Sunday on the Darkhovin nuclear facility in Iran's Khuzestan province, which Tehran has characterized as a civilian project under International Atomic Energy Agency safeguards.

key_facts.fact: The claim is unverified; neither Amazon, Bahraini authorities nor US officials confirmed it. Bahrain's military said it intercepted and destroyed a number of incoming projectiles but did not confirm any Amazon strike.
key_facts.excerpt: Bahrain's military said it had intercepted and destroyed a number of incoming projectiles. Bahraini authorities did not confirm any strike on an Amazon facility, and there was no official confirmation of any damage.

key_facts.fact: The IRGC also claimed it hit US military sites in Jordan, saying it destroyed a missile-defense radar system and a US Air Force F-15 fighter jet.
key_facts.excerpt: The IRGC also claimed that a missile defense radar system and a US Air Force F-15 fighter jet had both been destroyed in Jordan.

key_facts.fact: It is the second time in 2026 that Iran has claimed to strike Amazon-linked infrastructure in the Gulf.
key_facts.excerpt: This is the second time this year that Iran has claimed to have struck Amazon-linked infrastructure in the Gulf.

stories.headline: Russian strike kills 10 on grain ship near Odesa; Ukraine hits Moscow with 400+ drones

key_facts.fact: A Russian missile strike on a Guinea-Bissau-flagged ship carrying corn near Odesa killed at least 10 people on July 20; the crew was from India and Syria, and 8 crew members were rescued.
key_facts.excerpt: Russia struck a Guinea-Bissau-flagged ship carrying corn with a crew from India and Syria, Ukraine's seaports authority said on Monday. Officials said eight crew members had been rescued.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine launched hundreds of drones at the Moscow region overnight; Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said more than 400 drones flew toward the region between 20:30 Sunday and 5:00 Monday, with 85 downed near the capital and at least 10 people wounded, including a child.
key_facts.excerpt: Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said more than 400 'enemy drones' were launched at the Moscow region... He said 10 people, including a child, were wounded, and three of the wounded were Chinese citizens.

key_facts.fact: President Zelensky confirmed Ukrainian strikes hit an oil depot and logistics facilities more than 400 km inside Russia, plus two shadow-fleet tankers and four dry-cargo ships in the Black Sea.
key_facts.excerpt: Zelenskyy confirmed attacks on an oil depot and logistics facilities in the Moscow region on July 20, adding that two tankers from Russia's shadow fleet and four cargo ships also had been hit.

key_facts.fact: Russia said a Ukrainian strike on a bus in the Belgorod border region killed five civilians, including a minor, and critically injured three others.
key_facts.excerpt: Russia said Monday that a Ukrainian strike on a bus in the border region of Belgorod killed five civilians, including a minor, and left three others critically injured.

key_facts.fact: Russian attacks killed at least 14 people and injured over 160 across Ukraine over the past day, with the deadliest strikes in Zaporizhzhia (3 killed, 78+ injured) and Kharkiv oblasts.
key_facts.excerpt: Russian attacks killed at least 14 people and injured at least 162 across Ukraine over the past day, local authorities said on July 20, with the deadliest strikes reported in Zaporizhzhia and Kharkiv oblasts.

stories.headline: Iran vows no oil through Hormuz as Houthis threaten Saudi ports; Brent holds above $90

key_facts.fact: Iran's IRGC warned Monday (July 20) that 'not a single drop' of oil or gas would pass through the Strait of Hormuz as long as US 'aggression' continues.
key_facts.excerpt: The IRGC said, 'This passage will not be safe for the transit of petrochemical products, nor even a single drop of oil and gas.'

key_facts.fact: Brent crude briefly climbed as high as $91.01 a barrel intraday Monday and traded around $88-89, up roughly 13-16% over the prior month, while US gasoline pushed back above $4 a gallon.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude traded at $88.44 a barrel at 8:25 a.m. EDT on Monday, up 0.38% on the day and 13.57% over the past month. Prices briefly climbed as high as $91.01 earlier in the session.

key_facts.fact: Shipping through Hormuz collapsed to only 8 vessels on Sunday, a three-week low, down from around 130-140 per day before the US and Israel began strikes on Iran on Feb. 28, according to Kpler.
key_facts.excerpt: On Sunday, only eight vessels passed through the waterway — a three-week low — down from 15 the previous week... Before the US and Israel launched strikes against Iran on Feb. 28, between 130 and 140 vessels passed through the strait each day.

key_facts.fact: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said the country is 'engaged in a full-scale war' with the United States, while Tehran's Houthi allies said they would blockade Saudi ports.
key_facts.excerpt: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian described the country as 'engaged in a full-scale war' with the United States, while Tehran's Yemeni allies, the Houthi rebels, announced they would blockade Saudi ports.

key_facts.fact: The IRGC said two oil tankers 'exploded and were immobilised' after attempting to transit a southern route through the Strait of Hormuz.
key_facts.excerpt: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said on Monday that two oil tankers 'had exploded and been immobilised after attempting to transit through the southern route through the Strait of Hormuz.'

stories.headline: Anduril and Archer unveil 'Thunder' autonomous attack rotorcraft at Farnborough

key_facts.fact: On the opening day of the Farnborough Airshow (July 20), Anduril and Archer Aviation unveiled a jointly-developed series hybrid-electric VTOL platform; Anduril's military variant, 'Thunder,' is a Group 5 autonomous attack rotorcraft.
key_facts.excerpt: Anduril showcased the defense variant, Thunder, a Group 5 autonomous attack rotorcraft specifically designed to multiply the combat power of current and next-generation crewed attack and assault aircraft.

key_facts.fact: Thunder is designed to fly as a 'loyal wingman' in groups of three to six alongside crewed helicopters such as the Apache and future Cheyenne, using Anduril's Lattice for Mission Autonomy software.
key_facts.excerpt: Thunder... designed to be a 'loyal wingman' flying beside helicopters like the Apache and future Cheyenne fleet... primarily designed to fly in a group of three to six other Thunders alongside aircraft like an Apache or Cheyenne.

key_facts.fact: The design combines Karem Aircraft's optimum-speed tiltrotor technology, Archer's hybrid-electric drivetrain and Anduril's autonomy; surrogate test flights are complete, with Thunder's first flight planned for 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: The Thunder design... combines the optimum-speed tiltrotor technology of Karem Aircraft, the hybrid-electric drivetrain of electric-VTOL aircraft developer Archer Aviation, and Anduril's own autonomous control system.

key_facts.fact: Anduril is targeting first flight in 2027 and production in the 2029-2030 timeframe, positioning Thunder as an offering to the US Army and partner militaries.
key_facts.excerpt: He said the goal is to enter into production in the 2029 to 2030 timeframe, depending on demand from the US military, namely the Army, and partner militaries.

key_facts.fact: The companies also built a commercial version of the platform; Archer (NYSE: ACHR) will announce its first commercial partners later this week.
key_facts.excerpt: Archer will announce its first commercial partners for the platform later this week.

stories.headline: Ant International raises $1.2B in equity round backed by Ant Group and Alibaba

key_facts.fact: Ant International, the overseas affiliate of Jack Ma-founded Ant Group, said on Tuesday (July 21) it raised $1.2 billion in an equity funding round to accelerate global expansion.
key_facts.excerpt: Ant International, an overseas affiliate of the Jack Ma-founded Chinese fintech firm Ant Group, has raised $1.2 billion in its latest equity fundraising as it seeks to expand.

key_facts.fact: Affiliates Ant Group and Alibaba Group participated in the private round (undisclosed amounts), alongside other international investors.
key_facts.excerpt: Affiliates Ant Group and Alibaba Group participated in the private funding round, the company said on Tuesday, without disclosing the size of their commitment.

key_facts.fact: Ant International was valued at $10 billion prior to the round; the Singapore-based digital payments firm was spun out of China's Ant Group as an independent company in 2024.
key_facts.excerpt: Prior to the funding round, Ant International was valued at $10 billion, Reuters reported last month... The Singapore-based firm is a digital payments and fintech firm that was spun out of China's Ant Group as an independently operated company in 2024.

key_facts.fact: The firm says it connects more than 150 million merchants with over 2 billion user accounts across Asia, Europe, the Middle East and Latin America, and will use proceeds for merchant payments, account management, cross-border commerce and agentic commerce.
key_facts.excerpt: Ant International said its platform connects more than 150 million merchants with over 2 billion user accounts worldwide. The funding will also support Ant International's work in agentic commerce.

stories.headline: Tencent in talks to buy Playtika's SuperPlay for up to $1.5B

key_facts.fact: Tencent is in talks to acquire Israeli mobile-game studio SuperPlay from Playtika at a valuation of between $1 billion and $1.5 billion, per Calcalist.
key_facts.excerpt: Calcalist has learned that the mobile gaming company is negotiating the sale of Israeli game developer SuperPlay to Chinese giant Tencent in a deal valuing the company at between $1 billion and $1.5 billion.

key_facts.fact: Playtika bought SuperPlay in November 2024 for $690 million in cash plus an earnout of up to $1.25 billion tied to 2025-2027 performance; Tencent would assume the earnout, relieving Playtika of the liability.
key_facts.excerpt: Playtika acquired SuperPlay in November 2024 for $690 million in cash... The deal also included an earnout worth up to $1.25 billion... the Chinese company would assume responsibility for those payments, relieving Playtika of a liability.

key_facts.fact: SuperPlay, maker of Disney Solitaire and Dice Dreams, generated $573 million in revenue in 2025, roughly 67% above the baseline target used to calculate the earnout.
key_facts.excerpt: SuperPlay generated $573m in revenue in 2025, which is thought to be 67% above the 'baseline target used to calculate the earnout'.

key_facts.fact: Playtika's shares have lost roughly two-thirds of their value over three years, leaving the company with a market capitalization of about $1.5 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Playtika's stock has lost about two-thirds of its value over the past three years... the company is trading at a valuation of about $1.5 billion, roughly 80% below its peak.

stories.headline: Kolon TissueGene's cell-gene knee osteoarthritis therapy fails first US Phase 3 trial

key_facts.fact: Kolon TissueGene reported on July 20 topline results from ACTiVION-II, the first of two US Phase 3 trials of TG-C, a potential first-in-class cell and gene therapy for osteoarthritis of the knee; the trial did not meet its co-primary endpoints.
key_facts.excerpt: Kolon TissueGene... today announced topline results from the first of two US Phase 3 clinical trials of TG-C, a potential first-in-class cell and gene therapy targeting osteoarthritis of the knee (OAK)... did not meet the co-primary endpoints.

key_facts.fact: The 531-patient, 27-site trial showed TG-C did not significantly improve VAS pain or WOMAC total score versus placebo at Month 12, and it missed all key secondary endpoints.
key_facts.excerpt: The Phase 3 ACTiVION-II study enrolled 531 randomized subjects across 27 U.S. clinical trial sites. TG-C did not demonstrate statistically significant improvements versus placebo in pain and function... Additionally, the study did not meet any of the key secondary endpoints.

key_facts.fact: TG-C is a single intra-articular injection developed under an FDA Special Protocol Assessment; topline results from the second Phase 3 trial (ACTiVION-I) are anticipated in October 2026, after which the company will decide next steps.
key_facts.excerpt: Topline results from ACTiVION-I, the second Phase 3 clinical trial of TG-C... are anticipated in October 2026, after which Kolon TissueGene will determine next steps.
